manifest.name: dsh-intent-recognition
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: five-layer intent recognition (rules / vector / Jev / fine-tuned / LLM fallback). Zero-config basic edition (local file storage) out of the box; advanced edition adds PostgreSQL + pgvector vector retrieval. Scenario & service management UI included.

summary.en: Five-layer intent recognition pipeline. Basic edition works out of the box (local storage); advanced edition unlocks pgvector retrieval. Scenario/intent management UI and API services.
summary.zh: 五层意图识别流水线：规则/向量/Jev/微调/LLM兜底，场景与意图管理、PostgreSQL + pgvector 存储、API 服务。

scripts.test: node test/client-contract.mjs && node test/connection.mjs && node test/cordis-load.mjs && node test/smoke.mjs && node test/basic-mode.mjs
scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run typecheck && npm run build

bundle.text:
# dsh-intent-recognition bundle patch.
# `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-intent-recognition` applies this layer.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-intent-recognition
      name: dsh-intent-recognition
      config:
        # PostgreSQL connection string (FALLBACK). A connection saved from the
        # management page (意图识别 → 数据库) takes priority over this value and
        # is persisted to the per-user config dir; edit here only if you prefer
        # file-based provisioning. pgvector must be available (CREATE EXTENSION
        # vector). See docker-compose.yml.
        databaseUrl: postgres://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/dsh_intent
        # Embedding dimension of the configured vector model (must match the
        # embedding model actually used; changing it requires re-embedding).
        embeddingDim: 1024
        # Create tables/indexes automatically on plugin load.
        autoMigrate: true
        # Optional bearer token protecting the management API
        # (/dsh-intent-recognition/api/*). Empty = loopback web UI only.
        adminToken: ''

readme.text:
English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: five-layer intent recognition pipeline + scenario/intent management UI + dual-edition storage (basic = zero-config local file, advanced = PostgreSQL + pgvector) + distributable API services + DSH-native routing (agent tools / workflows / subagents / Cordis services).

```
User query
   │
   ▼
┌─ L1 rule hard filter ───────── greeting / exit / command / keyword strong match (lexicon + regex + black/white lists)
**Every layer can be toggled off per service** — disabled layers are skipped entirely.

- **Control plane (management UI)**: the **Intent Recognition** sidebar panel (same level as the Plugins entry; pin/unpin from the sidebar's More menu), plus a Settings → Intent Recognition section — both render the same management UI. Tooling only; it never joins the conversation.
- **Data plane (consumable services)**: a running service can be consumed two ways:

| Channel | Notes | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Agent tool** (recommended) | each running service registers `intent_recognize_<service-slug>`; high-confidence hits execute the route inside the tool | DSH main agent routing user turns |
| **Cordis service** | `ctx.intentRecognition.predict(service, query, context)` for other plugins | programmatic integration |

- **Zero-config start**: the basic edition (local file storage) is the default — install and build intents, models and services without any database. Upgrade to the advanced edition in-page whenever you need vector retrieval; existing data migrates automatically.
- **Intent management**: per-scenario intent catalog (name/code/description/examples/keywords/blacklist/whitelist/route config), Excel import (merge/replace) & export, one-click embedding rebuild (advanced).
- **Model configuration**: embedding, Jev, fine-tuned and LLM models are all page-configured (OpenAI-compatible or plain http JSON endpoints), with connectivity tests.
- **Service management**: per-scenario API services, independent switches & parameters per layer, services can **run / stop / delete / copy**; per-service API keys; built-in test console and call logs.
- **Vector lab** (advanced): a dedicated tab for layer-2 recall debugging — recall tests (type a question, see per-chunk scores and the aggregated intent candidate set, optionally inheriting a service's threshold/TopK), chunk browsing (example text / dims / building model / timestamp, with single-chunk delete), and per-scenario coverage overview with in-pl

Tabs follow the order of use: **Intents → Models → Services → Vector (advanced) → Database**. Until the first service exists, a three-step onboarding strip sits on top of the page; in the basic edition the Vector tab carries a 🔒 and opens an upgrade explainer.

All shots below show the **basic edition** (local storage, zero config) in real use:

| --- | --- |
|  |  |

| Model configuration (connectivity test) | Service management (chat tool registered) |

Prerequisites: Node.js ≥ 20, DSH installed (`npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh`). **No database needed** — the basic edition works out of the box.

readme.section: to upgrade — existing scenarios/intents/models/services migrate automatically
readme.text: > **When to switch editions**: start with the basic edition; upgrade on the Database tab when you need L2 vector retrieval. The switch is instant, local data migrates with ids and API keys preserved, and you can switch back to basic at any time — the local file stays untouched.

readme.section: to upgrade — existing scenarios/intents/models/services migrate automatically
readme.text: > **Desktop note**: if the sidebar entry is missing after install/upgrade, reload the page first (Ctrl+R or restart the app). The page loads the plugin client roster once at boot — the official plugin manager shows the same "refresh" prompt after installs. If the entry is still missing after a reload, check Settings → Intent Recognition: both come from the same client bundle, and if neither renders the client half never loaded — confirm the component shows "running" on the plugin detail page.

readme.section: to upgrade — existing scenarios/intents/models/services migrate automatically
readme.text:
> The sidebar entry registers through DSH's `sidebar.panellist` + `main` panel slots — the same mechanism as the built-in Plugins and Scheduled Tasks entries: clicking the icon opens the full management page in the main column, and the shell's More menu provides pin/unpin out of the box.

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` mounts it into the profile bundle stack automatically — no manual `cordis.patch.yml` editing.
Since v0.7.0 the plugin ships two storage editions; a banner on first open explains which one is active:

| | Basic (default) | Advanced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Storage | Local JSON file (next to the connection config, e.g. `data.json`) | PostgreSQL + pgvector |
| Database required | No — zero config | Yes (page-configured, instant effect) |
| L1 rules / L3 Jev / L4 fine-tuned / L5 LLM | ✅ | ✅ |
| L2 vector retrieval, vector lab, embedding rebuild | ❌ (tab shows 🔒; L2 is skipped at runtime with a trace note) | ✅ |
| Best for | trying things out, rule-driven catalogs | large intent libraries, diverse phrasings, semantic recall |

- **Upgrade**: fill in the PostgreSQL connection on the Database tab and "Test & Save". With "Migrate local data" on (default), existing scenarios/intents/models/services are copied into the database **keeping ids and API keys**, so agent tools and API callers notice nothing. Re-migration is idempotent (existing rows are skipped). Rebuild embeddings afterwards to enable L2.
- **Downgrade**: "Switch back to basic" on the Database tab returns storage to the local file — **local data stays exactly as it was before the upgrade** (rows created in advanced are not written back), and the connection config is kept for the next upgrade.
- **Edition resolution** (at boot): explicit basic choice > page-saved connection > patch `databaseUrl` (only if reachable) > basic fallback. The plugin always loads and the panel always opens.

The "Intent Recognition → Database" tab manages the edition and the advanced connection: a "Storage edition" card on top shows the current edition, the local data file path, and per-table row counts. In the advanced edition it offers a structured form (host/port/database/user/password/SSL) or a raw DSN, **Test connection** (also probes pgvector availability), **Test & Save** (persists + hot-swaps storage without any restart), **Clear page config** (fall back to the patch DSN or basic), **Switch back to basic**, and **Migrate local data into this database** (available whenever local rows exist).

While the database is unreachable (advanced edition), a red banner at the top of the panel guides you to the Database tab; saving hot-swaps storage and takes effect immediately:

| Disconnected banner | Database tab (connected) |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |

- **Priority**: explicit basic choice > page-saved DSN > `cordis.patch.yml` `databaseUrl` (only counts when reachable) > basic fallback. An unreachable page-saved DSN never silently falls back to basic (that would split your data) — the panel still opens, management routes answer 503, and you recover by fixing the connection or explicitly switching back to basic.
- **Persistence**: `%APPDATA%/dsh-intent-recognition/` (Windows), `~/Library/Application Support/dsh-intent-recognition/` (macOS), `~/.config/dsh-intent-recognition/` (Linux); override with the `DSH_INTENT_RECOGNITION_CONFIG` env var. Inside: `connection.json` (advanced DSN; password masked as `***` in API responses, submitting `***` keeps the stored one), `data.json` (basic-edition data), `storage.json` (explicit basic marker). All files are mode 0600.
- **pgvector**: with `autoMigrate` on, a successful save runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector` plus schema migration automatically; the test button warns beforehand when the target lacks pgvector. A database without pgvector can be connected, but L2 stays unavailable (the page says so).
- **Database maintenance**: below the connection form, **Check / Create / Drop da

| Field | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `databaseUrl` | `postgres://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/dsh_intent` | Advanced-edition fallback DSN (page-saved config wins; only counts when reachable, otherwise basic edition); pgvector must be available |
| `embeddingDim` | `1024` | Must match the configured embedding model; changing it requires an embedding rebuild |
| `autoMigrate` | `true` | Create tables/indexes on load (HNSW cosine index, pgvector ≥ 0.5) |
| `adminToken` | `''` | Bearer token protecting the management API; empty = DSH loopback only |
| `registerTool` | `true` | Register one `intent_recognize_<slug>` tool per running service |
| `contributePrompt` | `true` | Inject a system-prompt section listing available intent services |

| Route type | Config | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | — | Return the recognition result only |
| `workflow` | target (run name) + workflow script | Starts a DSH workflow run; the script orchestrates freely (call subagents, tools, other plugins) |
| `subagent` | target = **agent preset id** | Spawns a subagent with that preset to handle the query (`provider: spawn`, result returned to caller) |
| `service` | target = `serviceName.method` | Calls a method of another Cordis service in the host (capability provided by another plugin) |

- **auto (default)**: deterministic hits (L1 / L3 / L4) **execute the route inside the tool** — the cheap deterministic path actually lands; L5 (LLM fallback) hits only return the route as a suggestion for the main agent.
- **suggest**: never executes; the route is returned to the caller (agent or HTTP client).

Results carry `route` when configured; after execution they also carry `route_result` (`ok / value / error`).
With route type `workflow`, write the script directly in the intent editor (a collapsible full guide is built into the page). The script receives:

| Variable | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `args.query` | raw user input |
| `args.intent` | matched intent code |
| `args.confidence` | 0–1 |
| `args.matched_layer` | `l1`–`l5` |
| `args.slots` | slots extracted by L5 |
| `args.context` | caller-provided context array |
| `agent(prompt)` | spawn a subagent inside the script |
| `meta` | run metadata (`meta.name` = route target) |
The whole system treats DSH as the backbone — intent routing and downstream agents/workflows all attach as plugins:

1. **Workflows**: scripts live in the intent's route config and travel with the catalog via Excel import/export ("workflow script" column). Reuse capabilities via `agent()` or route type `service`.
2. **Subagents**: ship downstream capabilities as **agent preset** plugins (see `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset`); put the preset id in the route target.
3. **Cordis services**: a downstream plugin does `ctx.reflect.provide('xxxService', ...)` in `apply`; set the route target to `xxxService.methodName`. The method is called as `(result, exec)` where `result` carries query/intent/confidence/slots.

readme.section: Using services in the chat window (Agent tools)
readme.text: Once a service is **running**, the plugin registers a chat tool `intent_recognize_<slug>` with DSH (slug derived from the service name; revoked automatically when the service stops). From then on, just ask in any conversation — the main agent calls the tool when relevant and the route config dispatches to workflows / subagents / Cordis services. You can also invoke it explicitly, e.g. "use intent_recognize_bank_router to check: I want to transfer money".

readme.section: Using services in the chat window (Agent tools)
readme.text:
Each service card shows a "chat tool registered / not registered" badge; if registration fails (e.g. a name clash), the reason is shown under the badge. State syncs in real time with service start/stop.

> Note: tool registration is controlled by the `registerTool` plugin option (on by default) and requires the DSH `tools` service (present in web/desktop builds).
The Jev model dialog offers two **extra-config generators**; pick a scenario whose intents are configured, then choose:

- **AI generation**: calls a configured LLM (add one under model configuration first; if none is configured or the call fails, the error is surfaced — use the rule template instead). The full intent descriptions (definition / inclusion signals / exclusion rules / boundary distinctions, with examples) are passed to the model verbatim, and the prompt demands faithful preservation of those rules.
- **Rule template**: deterministic, no LLM required — embeds each intent's full description into `instructions` with generic five-band scoring criteria.

Both generate **all three judgment modes at once** (`modes.score` / `modes.choice` / `modes.noul`). Since v0.6.0 each mode carries **a single question named `intent_recognition`** that judges every candidate intent in one call:

| Mode | type | criteria | answer | score mapping |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| score | `score` | array of per-intent decision descriptions, plus `intent_order` (intent codes aligned 1:1 with criteria) | score array (in `intent_order` order) or `{code: score}` object | array indexes map via `intent_order` |
| choice | `choice` | `{intent name: decision description}` object | one intent name | chosen = 1, others = 0 |
| noul | `noul` | — (`map` binds “是”/“否” to the two intent codes) | “是”/“否” | per `map`: hit = 1, other = 0 |

> **noul is only generated for exactly-2-intent scenarios** — yes/no cannot cover more; don't pick noul as the layer-3 mode otherwise.

**Which mode runs is chosen per service**: the service editor's layer 3 has a "judgment mode" dropdown (score/choice/noul, default score); layer 3 then sends the corresponding `modes.<mode>` question. Legacy extra configs (per-intent `modes` questions, or a single top-level `questions`) keep working — layer 3 falls back to per-intent calls.

Layer-3 thresholds decide the outcome: **top score ≥ high threshold** → direct hit (skips L4/L5); **[mid, high)** → compressed candidates go to L4 arbitration; **below mid** → L5 fallback. The result is a draft — review it in the extra-config field before saving.

A Jev model with this extra config (`api_style=http`) switches layer 3 to the systemone wire format:

Score answers may be an array aligned with `intent_order`, a `{scores|values|results: [...]}` wrapper, or a `{code: score}` object; choice answers are an intent name (「」 quotes, codes, case and containment tolerant); noul answers are “是”/“否” mapped via the question's `map`. All three modes also accept object answers like `{choice: "name", confidence: 1, probabilities: {name: p}}` — `probabilities` maps are scored directly, otherwise the `choice`/`answer`/`value` label field is matched. Legacy per-intent answers `{"answers": {"<intent code>": ...}}` keep working: numbers, booleans, `"是"/"否"/"true"` strings, or `{score|probability|confidence}` objects.

The layer-2 "confidence threshold (min similarity)" (`minScore`) in the service editor is the slice filter — recalled chunks below it never become candidates. Test traces now expose it: layer 2 carries `minScore` / `topK` / `chunks` (every raw recalled slice with its score and pass/fail) / `candidates` (post-aggregation), so "recalled but not adopted" is directly attributable to threshold filtering vs aggregation truncation; layer 3 traces carry the judgment `mode`.

> Advanced-edition feature (requires pgvector). In the basic edition the tab shows 🔒 with an upgrade explainer; available after upgrading and rebuilding embeddings.

The **Vector Lab** tab answers "why was recall wrong for this question":

1. **Recall test**: pick a scenario, type any question, and the plugin replays the engine's real layer-2 logic (same `searchSimilar`, per-intent best chunk, minScore filter, TopK truncation). Optionally reference a service to inherit its embedding model and layer-2 threshold/TopK, or pick a model and tweak the threshold ad hoc. Two result tables: the **intent aggregation** (what layer 2 would actually emit downstream) and the **raw chunk hits** (every recalled slice with its score).
2. **Chunk browser**: all embedding slices of a scenario (example text, owning intent, dims, building model, build time), filterable by intent, paginated, with per-chunk delete for stale slices.
3. **Coverage overview**: per-scenario intent/example/chunk counts, coverage gaps, the models that built the slices, last rebuild time, and in-place rebuild with a chosen model.
Slices carry model provenance (`model_id`); after switching embedding models or editing examples, rebuild — otherwise old and new slices live in incompatible vector spaces.

Header row: `Name | Code | Description | Examples | Keywords | Blacklist | Whitelist | Route Type | Route Target | Workflow Script`. Multi-values inside examples are newline-separated, others use `、`; route type is `none / workflow / subagent / service` (a target or script without a type infers `workflow`). The exported file is the template.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck
pnpm build                     # emits lib/index.js + lib/client.js (esbuild)
node test/smoke.mjs            # end-to-end pipeline (needs local PostgreSQL+pgvector, see test/README.md)

Source layout: `src/index.ts` (host entry / Cordis integration), `src/pipeline/engine.ts` (five-layer engine), `src/dispatcher.ts` (route dispatch: workflow/subagent/service), `src/service-tools.ts` (per-service tool registration), `src/routes.ts` (REST API), `src/store.ts` (storage interface + basic-edition FileStore), `src/storage.ts` (edition management: resolution / upgrade migration / downgrade), `src/db.ts` (advanced PostgreSQL/pgvector, hot-swappable pool), `src/connection.ts` (page-managed connection), `src/models.ts` (model calls), `src/excel.ts` (import/export), `src/client/` (React management UI, `settings.section` + `main` + `sidebar.panellist` slots).
